Docs.param: The input connection on which to call the method.
The composing text. The default style for composing text is used.

The new cursor position around the text. If > 0, this is relative to the end of the text - 1; if <= 0, this is relative to the start of the text. So a value of 1 will always advance you to the position after the full text being inserted. Note that this means you can't position the cursor within the text, because the editor can make modifications to the text you are providing so it is not possible to correctly specify locations there.
Docs.summary: Replace the currently composing text with the given text, and set the new cursor position.
Docs.returns: The value returned by the input connection's character sequence overload.

remarks.para: Replace the currently composing text with the given text, and set the new cursor position. Any composing text set previously will be removed automatically.

If there is any composing span currently active, all characters that it comprises are removed. The passed text is added in its place, and a composing span is added to this text. If there is no composing span active, the passed text is added at the cursor position (removing selected characters first if any), and a composing span is added on the new text. Finally, the cursor is moved to the location specified by newCursorPosition.
Input methods usually call this method to add, remove, or change characters in the composing span. The editor calls on the current input method after the batch edit is over.

Editor authors: the text can be similar to or different from the current composing text, and there may be no composing span. An empty string replaces the composing text with empty text. Handle the cursor position as specified; input methods rely on it. Report the changes with , waiting until any batch edit is over. This method can set the cursor at either edge of the composing text or outside it. A later call can also move the cursor within the composing text; the composing text and selection are independent.
